root_cause.text: The `tlv_data_is_valid()` function performed bounds checking for each TLV element after reading `data[i+1]` (the type octet), allowing an out-of-bounds read when the length byte is the last byte of the buffer.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE description and commit message state that "tlv_data_is_valid() reads each advertising data field length from data[i], then inspects data[i + 1] for managed EIR types before checking that the current field still fits inside the supplied buffer. A malformed field whose length byte is the last byte of the buffer can therefore make the parser read one byte past the advertising data." The patch fixes this by moving the existing element-length check before any type-octet inspection.

intent_record.what: Added a conditional check that returns false if the current field length would cause the index to exceed or equal the total data length.
intent_record.how: Prevents out-of-bounds read access by validating that the field length does not extend beyond the data buffer before reading the next byte.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove an incorrect field length boundary check in tlv_data_is_valid due to a off-by-one error that could cause false rejections or allow out-of-bounds reads.
intent_record.what: Removed a conditional block that checked if the current field length would exceed the total data length and returned false if so, including its associated comment.
intent_record.how: The function no longer performs this boundary check, meaning that TLV fields with a length that would extend beyond the total data length will no longer be rejected by this specific check, potentially leading to out-of-bounds access if other validation is insufficient.
